newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 ends above 4,000 for the first time - OCT 2.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 ends above 4,000 for the first time - OCT 2.

text.p: The FTSE 100 sailed through the 4,000 mark with ease on Wednesday to close at a new record peak for the second day running as a strong international bond market and Wall Street strength pushed blue chip prices higher. The FTSE 100 ended at 4,015.1, up 22.9 points. Advancers beat decliners by a margin of more than two to one.

SEAQ volume was 721.5 million shares by 1537 GMT. The benchmark index has rallied some 380 points, or about 10.5 percent, since closing at year's low of 3632 on July 16. Today's record close marks the fifth since then.
Yet ironically, despite today surge, the FTSE 100 remains Europe's second worse performing index in Europe after Italy, noted David Aserkoff, a strategist with Credit First Boston.
"The UK market is fairly solid, but I don't see a huge amount of upside," said Aserkoff.
He thinks the FTSE will most likely top out around 4,050 to 4,100. "I think that's well within reach by year end."

An influx of cash at the start to the fourth quarter and robust bond markets on continuing signs of moderate inflationary pressures in the UK and U.S. have provided the backdrop for the market's rise in recent days.
Credit Lyonnais Laing strategist Cory Miller said dividends in coming weeks would be worth as much as three billion stg, and a substantial sum could be reinvested in the rising FTSE 100.

But unease at the current levels of London and New York markets and worries over a reluctance to raise interest rates ahead of elections on both sides of the Atlantic have some warning of sharp corrections ahead.

"We remain cautious looking into next year," said Nomura satrategist Nick Knight, "both as a function of our concerns regarding the U.S. and more particulary with regard to UK monetary policy post the election."
"To a certain extent what's good today may be bad tommorrow for the markets," he added.
Overnight comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that there were no threats to inflation down the track added to the upbeat mood in London markets from the start.
Large institutional cash holdings are widely seen as having been the main dynamo behind the recent rises and are expected by many to continue to power the market.
"In the very short term, it does appear there's quite a lot of cash sitting on the sidelines waiting to come in," said Panmure Gordon strategist Ian Williams.

"On a week-to-two week view there's probably more upside to come... over the fourth quarter as a whole we're still a little bit nervous but the underlying liquidity driver is going to be the factor in the near future," Williams said.
The UK market's charge to another record was mirrored on Wall Street overnight where the Dow broke 5,900 for the first time and looked to have 6,000 squarely in its sights.
The Dow was up some 24 points to 5,929 as London markets closed.
The next big hurdle for markets on both sides of the Atlantic is the U.S. payroll data due for release on Friday.
Among individual stocks, Kwik Save jumped 20-1/2p to 332p on speculation of a merger with Iceland.
ICI gained gained 19p to 877-1/2p after Merrill Lynch rated the stock a technical "buy."
--Debra Sherman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4026
